statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-39835 (GO-2026-5015, GHSA-78mq-xcr3-xm33): an SSH server built on golang.org/x/crypto/ssh that uses CertChecker as its public key callback without setting IsUserAuthority or IsHostAuthority panics when a client presents a certificate. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0, which makes CertChecker return an error instead (the fix changes ssh/certs.go), and the Go vulnerability database names CertChecker.Authenticate and CertChecker.CheckHostKey as the vulnerable functions: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5015, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-78mq-xcr3-xm33, https://go.dev/issue/79563, https://go.dev/cl/781660 Read every published alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 to the current 0.35.0-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the checksum in the package index. Each package installs two files, /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, Go programs built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and with -ldflags -s -w, as their Go build information records, so their functions were read from each binary's Go function table (pclntab), which lists runtime.main in every binary. Every binary was also searched as raw bytes for the package-qualified names, which also finds functions the compiler inlined. golang.org/x/crypto is v0.47.0 in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r3, v0.49.0 in 0.31.1-r4, v0.50.0 in 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r1, v0.52.0 in 0.32.1-r2 to 0.32.2-r0, and v0.53.0 to v0.58.0 in every later build, as listed in the Go build information of both programs. The only golang.org/x/crypto packages either program links are bcrypt and blowfish (alertmanager) and bcrypt (amtool). No binary in any build has a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh function in its function table or contains the package-qualified name golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, so the vulnerable code is not present. As a positive control, the same function-table reader and byte search, run on a test program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and -ldflags -s -w for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.50.0 and golang.org/x/net v0.53.0, which uses CertChecker.Authenticate as a server's public key callback and CertChecker.CheckHostKey as a client's host key callback, finds golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.(*CertChecker).Authenticate and (*CertChecker).CheckHostKey in the function table and both names in the byte search.

CVE-2026-39835 (GO-2026-5015, GHSA-78mq-xcr3-xm33): an SSH server using the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh CertChecker as its public key callback without setting IsUserAuthority or IsHostAuthority could be made to panic by a client presenting a certificate. The vulnerable code is CertChecker.Authenticate and CertChecker.CheckHostKey (the functions GO-2026-5015 lists), fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5015, https://go.dev/issue/79563, https://go.dev/cl/781660, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI. We read every published build-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 91 versions, 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.30.0-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64 (2.6.4-r0 is published for aarch64 only), after verifying each download against its index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times for each architecture in the package index; the one copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one program, the Go frontend program /usr/bin/build, besides the apk metadata. For every Go program in every build we read the function table (pclntab) and searched the binary's strings; each program's function table contains runtime.main. /usr/bin/build records golang.org/x/crypto v0.45.0 to v0.59.0 depending on the build and uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh as an SSH client only: its function table has NewClientConn and the client authentication code, and in no build does its function table or its strings contain any CertChecker method. As a check, the same function-table reader and strings search find NewServerConn, the connection's serverAuthenticate method, CertChecker.Authenticate and CertChecker.CheckHostKey in a test program built against golang.org/x/crypto v0.51.0 for x86_64 and aarch64. The vulnerable code is not present, so the golang.org/x/crypto version recorded in the build information does not make this package affected.

CVE-2026-39835 (GO-2026-5015, GHSA-78mq-xcr3-xm33): a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh server or client that used CertChecker without IsUserAuthority or IsHostAuthority set could be made to panic by a peer presenting a certificate, because CertChecker.Authenticate and CertChecker.CheckHostKey called the unset callback. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 by commit ffd87b4 (CL 781660, which names CVE-2026-39835): https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5015, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-78mq-xcr3-xm33, https://go.dev/issue/79563, https://go.dev/cl/781660, https://github.com/golang/crypto/commit/ffd87b4878fa. The Go vulnerability database lists the vulnerable functions as the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh methods CertChecker.Authenticate and CertChecker.CheckHostKey. We read every published external-dns-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 33 builds, 0.20.0-r0 to the current 0.24.0-r5, each for x86_64 and aarch64 and each matching its repository index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/external-dns (a full listing, symlinks included), a statically linked Go program (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies) built with CGO_ENABLED=0. Its Go build information lists golang.org/x/crypto v0.45.0 in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.20.0-r3, v0.49.0 in 0.20.0-r4 to 0.21.0-r1, v0.50.0 in 0.21.0-r2 and 0.21.0-r3, v0.51.0 in 0.21.0-r4, and v0.52.0 or later from 0.21.0-r5 on (v0.58.0 in the current build), with no replace directive for it, so the builds before 0.21.0-r5 are in the advisory's version range. The program does not contain the vulnerable code. A Go function-table (pclntab) reader finds runtime.main in every build, which shows the listing works on that file, but no function of the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package and none of golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent in any build: the only name under golang.org/x/crypto/ssh is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/terminal.init, the initializer of the separate ssh/terminal package, in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r13. A byte search of every build, which also catches the names of inlined functions, finds no "golang.org/x/crypto/ssh." at all. As a positive control, the same reader and byte search find ssh.(*CertChecker).Authenticate and ssh.(*CertChecker).CheckHostKey in a test program we built against golang.org/x/crypto v0.51.0, the last release before the fix, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The golang.org/x/crypto version in the build information therefore does not make this package affected.
